title: Sharp Communication Cost of Target Pilots for Transported ATE Estimation
banked_reason: The theorem proves the advertised exact one-half normalized pilot threshold, but only on the tuned slice d approximately N^{1/3}, B=(1/2)log_2 N+O(1), fixed C>1, and risk constants above a loose achievability constant; it does not establish a general dimension or two-budget communication frontier.
gap_reasons: The theorem proves the advertised exact one-half normalized pilot threshold, but only on the tuned slice d approximately N^{1/3}, B=(1/2)log_2 N+O(1), fixed C>1, and risk constants above a loose achievability constant; it does not establish a general dimension or two-budget communication frontier.
The econometric significance remains narrow because FACE is only motivation and no observational or federated estimator is shown to satisfy this benchmark.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a rounded-count upper protocol and a centered-chain all-protocol lower bound, yielding the sharp one-half normalized pilot threshold on the specified sampled-mass slice. The math referee passed, but the cold referee graded the research package subfield against the required field floor; a field result would require a broader communication frontier or a causal application theorem. Formalization did not start, and the mechanical related-work finding remains open.
tldr: Fix \(b_0\in\mathbb Z\) and \(N\ge N_0(b_0)=\max\{8,2^{-2b_0}\}\). On the slice \(d=2\lfloor N^{1/3}/2\rfloor\) and \(B_N=\lceil(\log_2N)/2\rceil+b_0\), the minimum target-pilot length attaining worst-case transported-ATE mean squared error \(C_0/N\) has the sharp normalization \(L_N^*(C_0)/\{d\log_2(N/d)\}\to1/2\) for every fixed \(C>1\) and fixed \(C_0\ge K_{\mathrm{up}}(C,b_0)\). Exact finite-coin stochastic count rounding and enumerative coding attain the upper coefficient. A full-dimensional centered-chain prior on the zero-sum subspace and an adaptive conditional entropy--covariance argument give the matching all-protocol converse while both mass vectors remain unknown and sampled.
gap: Generic distributed expectation and inner-product results begin with supplied laws or vectors, while causal transport methods exchange exact summaries. Neither literature determines the target-pilot bits required when both populations are observed only through independent samples and the return message is short.
fill: The project proves a computable finite-sample upper bound and a matching-order all-protocol lower bound on the same sampled causal class, then isolates the exact leading constant as the remaining information-theoretic object.
